verses.zh: 示巴女王听见所罗门的名声，就来到耶路撒冷，要用难解的话试问所罗门；跟随她的人甚多，又有骆驼驮着香料、宝石，和许多金子。她来见了所罗门，就把心里所有的对所罗门都说出来。
verses.en: When the queen of Sheba heard about Solomon,[NOTE:1] she came to challenge[NOTE:2] him[NOTE:3] with difficult questions.[NOTE:4] She arrived in Jerusalem[NOTE:5] with a great display of pomp,[NOTE:6] bringing with her camels carrying spices,[NOTE:7] a very large quantity of gold, and precious gems. She visited Solomon and discussed with him everything that was on her mind.
notes: Heb “the report about Solomon.”
Or “test.”
Heb “Solomon.” The recurrence of the proper name here is redundant in terms of contemporary English style, so the pronoun has been used in the translation instead.
Or “riddles.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “with very great strength.” The Hebrew word חַיִל (khayil, “strength”) may refer here to the size of her retinue or to the great wealth she brought with her.
Or “balsam oil.”

verses.zh: 所罗门将她所问的都答上了，没有一句不明白、不能答的。
verses.en: Solomon answered all her questions; there was no question too complex for the king.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Solomon declared to her all her words; there was not a word hidden from the king which he did not declare to her.” If riddles are specifically in view (see v. 1), then one might translate, “Solomon explained to her all her riddles; there was no riddle too complex for the king.”

verses.zh: 示巴女王见所罗门的智慧和他所建造的宫室、
verses.en: When the queen of Sheba saw for herself Solomon’s wisdom, the palace[NOTE:1] he had built,
notes: Heb “house.”

verses.zh: 席上的珍馐美味、群臣分列而坐、仆人两旁侍立，以及他们的衣服装饰、酒政，和酒政的衣服装饰，又见他上耶和华殿的台阶，就诧异得神不守舍，
verses.en: the food in his banquet hall,[NOTE:1] his servants and attendants[NOTE:2] in their robes, his cupbearers in their robes, and his burnt sacrifices which he presented in the Lord’s temple,[NOTE:3] she was amazed.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “the food on his table.”
Heb “the seating of his servants and the standing of his attendants.”

The Hebrew text has here, “and his upper room [by] which he was going up to the house of the Lord.” But עֲלִיָּתוֹ (ʿaliyyato, “his upper room”) should be emended to עֹלָתוֹ, (ʿolato, “his burnt sacrifice[s]”). See the parallel account in 1 Kgs 10:5.
Or “it took her breath away”; Heb “there was no breath still in her.”

verses.zh: 对王说：「我在本国里所听见论到你的事和你的智慧实在是真的！
verses.en: She said to the king, “The report I heard in my own country about your wise sayings and insight[NOTE:1] was true!
notes: Heb “about your words [or perhaps, “deeds”] and your wisdom.”

verses.zh: 我先不信那些话，及至我来亲眼见了，才知道你的大智慧；人所告诉我的，还不到一半；你的实迹越过我所听见的名声。
verses.en: I did not believe these things until I came and saw them with my own eyes. Indeed, I didn’t hear even half the story![NOTE:1] Your wisdom surpasses what was reported to me.
notes: Heb “the half was not told to me.”

verses.zh: 你的群臣、你的仆人常侍立在你面前听你智慧的话是有福的。
verses.en: Your attendants, who stand before you at all times and hear your wise sayings, are truly happy![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “How happy are your men! How happy are these servants of yours, who stand before you continually, who hear your wisdom!”

verses.zh: 耶和华―你的　神是应当称颂的！他喜悦你，使你坐他的国位，为耶和华―你的　神作王；因为你的　神爱以色列人，要永远坚立他们，所以立你作他们的王，使你秉公行义。」
verses.en: May the Lord your God be praised because he favored[NOTE:1] you by placing you on his throne as the one ruling on his behalf.[NOTE:2] Because of your God’s love for Israel and his lasting commitment to them,[NOTE:3] he made you king over them so you could make just and right decisions.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “delighted in.”
Heb “as king for the Lord your God.”
Heb “to make him stand permanently.”
Heb “to do justice and righteousness.”

verses.zh: 于是示巴女王将一百二十他连得金子和宝石，与极多的香料送给所罗门王；她送给王的香料，以后再没有这样的。
verses.en: She gave the king 120 talents[NOTE:1] of gold and a very large quantity of spices and precious gems. The quantity of spices the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon has never been matched.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew word כִּכַּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or, by extension, to a standard unit of weight. According to the older (Babylonian) standard the “talent” weighed 130 lbs. (58.9 kg), but later this was lowered to 108.3 lbs. (49.1 kg). More recent research suggests the “light” standard talent was 67.3 lbs. (30.6 kg). Using this as the standard for calculation, the weight of the gold was 8,076 lbs. (3,672 kg).
Heb “there has not been like those spices which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.”

verses.zh: 希兰的仆人和所罗门的仆人从俄斐运了金子来，也运了檀香木（或译：乌木；下同）和宝石来。
verses.en: (Huram’s[NOTE:1] servants, aided by Solomon’s servants, brought gold from Ophir, as well as[NOTE:2] fine[NOTE:3] timber and precious gems.
notes: Heb “Huram’s” (also in v. 21). Some medieval Hebrew mss, along with the LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate spell the name “Hiram,” agreeing with 1 Chr 14:1. “Huram” is a variant spelling referring to the same individual.
Heb “who brought gold from Ophir, brought.”
Heb “algum.”

verses.zh: 王用檀香木为耶和华殿和王宫做台，又为歌唱的人做琴瑟；犹大地从来没有见过这样的。
verses.en: With the timber the king made steps[NOTE:1] for the Lord’s temple and royal palace as well as stringed instruments[NOTE:2] for the musicians. No one had seen anything like them in the land of Judah before that.[NOTE:3])
notes: Heb “tracks.” The parallel text in 1 Kgs 10:12 has a different term whose meaning is uncertain: “supports,” perhaps “banisters” or “parapets.”
Two types of stringed instruments are specifically mentioned in the Hebrew text, the כִּנּוֹר (kinnor, “zither”) and נֶבֶל (nevel, “harp”).
Heb “there was not seen like these formerly in the land of Judah.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王按示巴女王所带来的，还她礼物，另外照她一切所要所求的，都送给她。于是女王和她臣仆转回本国去了。
verses.en: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she requested, more than what she had brought him.[NOTE:1] Then she left and returned[NOTE:2] to her homeland with her attendants.
notes: Heb “besides what she brought to the king.”
Heb “turned and went.”

verses.zh: 所罗门每年所得的金子共有六百六十六他连得，
verses.en: Solomon received 666 talents[NOTE:1] of gold per year,[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew word כִּכַּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or, by extension, to a standard unit of weight. According to the older (Babylonian) standard the “talent” weighed 130 lbs. (58.9 kg), but later this was lowered to 108.3 lbs. (49.1 kg). More recent research suggests the “light” standard talent was 67.3 lbs. (30.6 kg). Using this as the standard for calculation, the weight of the gold Solomon received annually was 44,822 lbs. (20,380 kg).
Heb “the weight of the gold which came to Solomon in one year was 666 talents of gold.”

verses.zh: 另外还有商人所进的金子，并且阿拉伯诸王与属国的省长都带金银给所罗门。
verses.en: besides what he collected from the merchants[NOTE:1] and traders. All the Arabian kings and the governors of the land also brought gold and silver to Solomon.
notes: Heb “traveling men.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王用锤出来的金子打成挡牌二百面，每面用金子六百舍客勒；
verses.en: King Solomon made 200 large shields of hammered gold; 600 measures[NOTE:1] of hammered gold were used for each shield.
notes: The Hebrew text has simply “600,” with no unit of measure given.

verses.zh: 又用锤出来的金子打成盾牌三百面，每面用金子三百舍客勒，都放在黎巴嫩林宫里。
verses.en: He also made 300 small shields of hammered gold; 300 measures[NOTE:1] of gold were used for each of those shields. The king placed them in the Palace of the Lebanon Forest.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew text has simply “300,” with no unit of measure given.

This name was appropriate because of the large amount of cedar, undoubtedly brought from Lebanon, used in its construction. The cedar pillars in the palace must have given it the appearance of a forest. See 1 Kgs 7:2.

verses.zh: 王用象牙制造一个大宝座，用精金包裹。
verses.en: The king made a large throne decorated with ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.

verses.zh: 宝座有六层台阶，又有金脚凳，与宝座相连。宝座两旁有扶手，靠近扶手有两个狮子站立。
verses.en: There were six steps leading up to the throne, and a gold footstool was attached to the throne.[NOTE:1] The throne had two armrests with a statue of a lion standing on each side.[NOTE:2]
notes: The parallel text of 1 Kgs 10:19 has instead “and the back of it was rounded on top.”
Heb “[There were] armrests on each side of the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests.”

verses.zh: 六层台阶上有十二个狮子站立，每层有两个：左边一个，右边一个；在列国中没有这样做的。
verses.en: There were twelve statues of lions on the six steps, one lion at each end of each step. There was nothing like it in any other kingdom.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “nothing like it had been made for any kingdom.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王一切的饮器都是金的，黎巴嫩林宫里的一切器皿都是精金的。所罗门年间，银子算不了甚么。
verses.en: All of King Solomon’s cups were made of gold, and all the household items in the Palace of the Lebanon Forest were made of pure gold. There were no silver items, for silver was not considered very valuable in Solomon’s time.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “there was no silver regarded as anything in the days of Solomon.”

verses.zh: 因为王的船只与希兰的仆人一同往他施去；他施船只三年一次装载金、银、象牙、猿猴、孔雀回来。
verses.en: The king had a fleet of large merchant ships[NOTE:1] manned by Huram’s men[NOTE:2] that sailed the sea. Once every three years the fleet[NOTE:3] came into port with cargoes of[NOTE:4] gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “for ships belonging to the king were going [to] Tarshish.” This probably refers to large ships either made in or capable of traveling to the distant western port of Tarshish.
Heb “servants.”
Heb “the fleet of Tarshish [ships].”
Heb “the ships of Tarshish came carrying.”
The meaning of this word is unclear; some suggest it refers to “baboons.” NEB has “monkeys,” NASB, NRSV “peacocks,” and NIV “baboons.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王的财宝与智慧胜过天下的列王。
verses.en: King Solomon was wealthier and wiser than any of the kings of the earth.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “King Solomon was greater than all the kings of the earth with respect to wealth and wisdom.”

verses.zh: 普天下的王都求见所罗门，要听　神赐给他智慧的话。
verses.en: All the kings of the earth wanted to visit Solomon to see him display his God-given wisdom.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and all the kings of the earth were seeking the face of Solomon to hear his wisdom which God had placed in his heart.”

verses.zh: 他们各带贡物，就是金器、银器、衣服、军械、香料、骡马，每年有一定之例。
verses.en: Year after year visitors brought their gifts, which included items of silver, items of gold, clothes, perfume, spices, horses, and mules.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they were bringing each one his gift, items of silver…and mules, the matter of a year in a year.”

verses.zh: 所罗门有套车的马四千棚，有马兵一万二千，安置在屯车的城邑和耶路撒冷，就是王那里。
verses.en: Solomon had 4,000 stalls for his chariot horses[NOTE:1] and 12,000 horses. He kept them in assigned cities and also with him in Jerusalem.[NOTE:2]
notes: The parallel text of 1 Kgs 10:26 reads “fourteen hundred chariots.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.tn Heb “he placed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.”

verses.zh: 所罗门统管诸王，从大河到非利士地，直到埃及的边界。
verses.en: He ruled all the kingdoms from the Euphrates River[NOTE:1] to the land of the Philistines as far as the border of Egypt.
notes: Heb “the River.” In biblical Hebrew the Euphrates River was typically referred to simply as “the River.”

verses.zh: 王在耶路撒冷使银子多如石头，香柏木多如高原的桑树。
verses.en: The king made silver as plentiful[NOTE:1] in Jerusalem as stones; cedar was[NOTE:2] as plentiful as sycamore fig trees are in the foothills.[NOTE:3]
notes: The words “as plentiful” are supplied for clarification.
Heb “he made cedar.”
The foothills (שְׁפֵלָה, shephelah) are the region between the Judean hill country and the Mediterranean coastal plain.

verses.zh: 有人从埃及和各国为所罗门赶马群来。
verses.en: Solomon acquired horses from Egypt and from all the lands.

verses.zh: 所罗门其余的事，自始至终，不都写在先知拿单的书上和示罗人亚希雅的预言书上，并先见易多论尼八儿子耶罗波安的默示书上吗？
verses.en: The rest of the events of Solomon’s reign, from start to finish, are recorded[NOTE:1] in the Annals of Nathan the Prophet, the Prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and the Vision of Iddo the Seer pertaining to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
notes: Heb “As for the rest of the events of Solomon, the former and the latter, are they not written?”

verses.zh: 所罗门在耶路撒冷作以色列众人的王共四十年。
verses.en: Solomon ruled over all Israel from Jerusalem[NOTE:1] for forty years.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 所罗门与他列祖同睡，葬在他父大卫城里。他儿子罗波安接续他作王。
verses.en: Then Solomon passed away[NOTE:1] and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam replaced him as king.
notes: Heb “lay down with his fathers.”
